comment: Recognition layer 3: landmark popups. Coordinates are real OSM lat/lon, projected into world space via the route origin+scale at load. radius = trigger distance in compressed-world units. Each landmark has a stable id from creation (standing rule — the future ad system depends on this pattern). category drives popup border colour and narrator event selection. needs_owner_review: true = map-research coords only; owner's lived knowledge is authoritative.

landmarks.name: Norman Manley International Airport
landmarks.fact: Jamaica's main international gateway — named after National Hero and first Chief Minister Norman Washington Manley

landmarks.name: Gun Boat Beach
landmarks.fact: Harbour-side bathing spot on the Palisadoes strip — calm water on the left, open sea on the right

landmarks.name: Port Royal
landmarks.fact: Once the wickedest city on earth — the pirate capital that sank into the sea in 1692

landmarks.name: Harbour View Roundabout
landmarks.fact: Where the Palisadoes meets the city — Kingston Harbour opens up to your left

landmarks.name: National Stadium
landmarks.fact: Home of Jamaican track and football glory — Excelsior High is just across Mountain View Avenue

landmarks.name: Excelsior High School
landmarks.fact: Opposite the National Stadium on Mountain View Avenue — powerhouse of Jamaican athletics and academics

landmarks.name: National Heroes Park
landmarks.fact: Resting place of Jamaica's National Heroes — Marcus Garvey, Norman Manley, Alexander Bustamante and more

landmarks.name: Jamaica College
landmarks.fact: Old Hope Road — one of Jamaica's most celebrated high schools, home of the 'Old Boys'

landmarks.name: Bob Marley Museum
landmarks.fact: 56 Hope Road — the Tuff Gong's home, studio and spiritual centre, now a museum visited by fans worldwide

landmarks.name: Devon House
landmarks.fact: 1881 mansion of George Stiebel, Jamaica's first black millionaire — and legendary ice cream

landmarks.name: Tracks & Records
landmarks.fact: Usain Bolt's restaurant on Constant Spring Road — world's fastest man, world's best jerk chicken?

landmarks.name: Emancipation Park
landmarks.fact: New Kingston's green heart — the Redemption Song sculpture marks Jamaica's journey from slavery to freedom

landmarks.name: Half Way Tree Clock Tower
landmarks.fact: The 1813 clock tower at the crossroads of Kingston

landmarks.name: St. Andrew High School
landmarks.fact: Half Way Tree area — top all-girls school, sister school to Kingston College

landmarks.name: Holy Childhood High School
landmarks.fact: Half Way Tree area — Catholic girls' school with deep roots in Jamaican education

landmarks.name: KFC Half Way Tree
landmarks.fact: KFC Jamaica — among the highest-grossing KFC locations anywhere in the world

landmarks.name: Tastee Patties
landmarks.fact: The original Jamaican patty — Tastee has been feeding Kingston since 1966

landmarks.name: Juici Patties
landmarks.fact: Juici Patties — the great patty rivalry lives on every lunchtime in Kingston

landmarks.name: Burger King
landmarks.fact: New Kingston — Burger King Jamaica, a favourite stop on the Half Way Tree strip

landmarks.name: Calabar High School
landmarks.fact: Red Hills Road — Baptist-founded school, one of Jamaica's leading boys' high schools

landmarks.name: Hydel High School
landmarks.fact: Leaving the city heading west — Hydel's athletics programme has punched well above its weight

landmarks.name: Flat Bridge
landmarks.fact: Historic one-lane bridge over the Rio Cobre in Bog Walk gorge

landmarks.name: Faith's Pen
landmarks.fact: Legendary roadside stop — jerk chicken, roast yam and festival since before anyone can remember

landmarks.name: Fern Gully
landmarks.fact: A natural tunnel of ferns and bamboo — the most photographed road in Jamaica

landmarks.name: Ocho Rios Bay
landmarks.fact: The Caribbean coast opens up — you made it to Ocho Rios

landmarks.name: Dunn's River Falls
landmarks.fact: Jamaica's famous climbable waterfall — journey's end
